claims.text: Kaiord for TrainingPeaks is the Chrome extension that connects the Kaiord App to TrainingPeaks; its Chrome Web Store name is Kaiord TrainingPeaks Bridge. Here is how it handles data:

proof.title: should POST the workout to the v6 endpoint with a Bearer header

claims.text: **No Password**: The extension never asks for, reads, stores, or transmits your TrainingPeaks password. It reuses the session you already established by signing in to TrainingPeaks in your browser.

proof.title: sends the cookie, and no Authorization header, to that endpoint

claims.text: **Access Token**: The extension exchanges your session cookie for a short-lived access token with a single cookie-only request, `GET https://tpapi.trainingpeaks.com/users/v3/token` (`credentials:"include"`, no `Authorization` header). The `Production_tpAuth` session cookie is a domain-wide `.trainingpeaks.com` cookie, so the browser attaches it to that request; the extension cannot read its value, because it does not declare the `cookies` permission. The extension keeps the token, the time it expires and your TrainingPeaks athlete number in `chrome.storage.local`.

proof.title: sends the cookie, and no Authorization header, to that endpoint
should mint a token and keep it in chrome.storage.local when the session is checked

claims.text: **Token Stays in Your Browser**: The token is sent only to TrainingPeaks, as a Bearer credential, and never travels to Kaiord: no answer the extension gives the Kaiord App contains it. Removing the extension from Chrome deletes it.

proof.title: should answer no external action with the token, when TrainingPeaks answers
should answer no external action with the token, when TrainingPeaks refuses the token
should send requests to tpapi.trainingpeaks.com only, and nothing anywhere else
should POST the workout to the v6 endpoint with a Bearer header

claims.text: **Checking the Connection**: Every time the Kaiord App or the popup checks your sign-in, the extension asks TrainingPeaks for a new token and stores it, and gives the Kaiord App your athlete number, which it needs to place a workout.

should never expose the access token in the probe response

It cannot delete anything in TrainingPeaks or change a workout already there: sending a changed workout again adds a second copy, and the Kaiord App asks you first.

The answer may include metrics other than weight, such as pulse, sleep or steps; the Kaiord App keeps only your weight. The extension also accepts a request to add one weight measurement, but the Kaiord App does not send it today. These are the `read:body`, `write:body` and `write:workouts` capabilities.
